structure: Part 18, Document scan status and the client-side enhancements. Read in full on main: documents/scan/status.js (54 lines: reading each upload's scan status from the document upload service, the pending fallback, the scanned list the status route returns, the rejected-by-scan helpers) and scan/summary-errors.js (15 lines: one error-summary entry per rejected document); documents/scan-poll.js (36 lines: the three scan states, the 3-second interval, the 10-try limit and the settled, retry or give-up decision); documents/download-content-type.js (24 lines: the content type and presentation a downloaded file is served with); all 12 files under documents/client/ (430 lines): index.js (drop zone set-up order), dom.js (element builder), restored-page.js (reopen on back/forward), scan-status/page.js, poll.js, status-cell.js and announce.js (the poll, the in-place row rewrite and the live-region announcements), and oversize-validation/control.js, submit.js, error-summary.js, field-error.js and markers.js (the in-browser 50MB check, its error summary and field error); the fit specs fit/scan-status.fit.spec.js (4 tests: settles on return, virus found until removed, axe on the settled table, in-place polling update) and fit/drop-zone.fit.spec.js (6 tests: button and instruction, no file chosen live region, drop reaches the input, single input named file, failed attachment drawn on the zone, axe); and copy/copy.en.js and copy.cy.js, claiming only the scan-status, announcement, drop-zone, view-file, refresh, still-checking, oversize, rejected and later-step scan keys, with the Welsh read for key parity. The *.test.js unit tests were not read, as the scope says. The code is unchanged from the earlier extract for the claims kept; the status tag colours, the status route's handler, the template's no-JavaScript fallbacks, the 50MB constant and the server-side oversize error now sit in files part 17 reads, so their earlier claims moved to part 17 and this part claims only the wording and behaviour its own files show.

claims.statement: A document the service has uploaded is in exactly one of three scan states: complete, pending or rejected.
A document row that holds no uploaded file is treated as having a completed scan, so it shows no scanning status.
When the service cannot read a document's scan status it shows the document as still being scanned rather than failing the page.
claims.note: The failure is logged at warn with the journey id and upload id.

claims.statement: The page reads each uploaded document's scan status from the document upload service, passing the document's file name with the upload identifier.
The browser asks for the scan statuses every 3 seconds, starting 3 seconds after the page opens.
claims.quote:
export const POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 3000
...
  setTimeout(() => pollScanStatus(0, scanCopy), POLL_INTERVAL_MS)

claims.statement: The browser asks for the scan statuses at most 10 times.
claims.quote:
export const MAX_POLL_ATTEMPTS = 10
...
const lastAttempt = (attempt) => attempt + 1 >= MAX_POLL_ATTEMPTS

claims.statement: Asking stops as soon as no document is still being scanned.
Once every scan has settled the browser opens the documents page again so the page is rebuilt with the settled statuses, the Continue state and any rejection errors.
A request for the scan statuses that fails, is refused or answers with something unusable counts as one of the 10 attempts and the browser tries again after the interval.
When the 10 attempts run out with a document still being scanned, the page shows the hint "Still checking some documents. Refresh again in a moment."
claims.note: copy.stillChecking is 'Still checking some documents. Refresh again in a moment.'

claims.statement: When the browser starts asking for statuses itself, the "Refresh virus scan status" link is hidden, so only one way of refreshing is offered at a time.
The browser starts asking for statuses only when the page shows at least one document still being scanned.
A screen-reader user is told when a document's scan completes: "Document scan complete: the file is safe to use".
claims.quote: safe: 'Document scan complete: the file is safe to use',

claims.statement: A status is announced only when it has actually changed, so a repeated answer does not repeat the announcement.
When a scan settles the row's status tag is rewritten where it stands, keeping the rest of the row and the hidden document label as they were.
When a scan completes without a reload, the row gains a "View file" link beside its Remove button.
A document whose scan settles as rejected offers no "View file" link, only Remove.
The "View file" link a settled row gains carries a visually hidden suffix naming which document it is for, and opens the file under the documents page's own path.

claims.statement: The service can say whether any document on a notification was rejected by the scan, and list the rejected ones.
claims.quote:
export const isRejectedByScan = (item) =>
  item.scanStatus === SCAN_STATUS.REJECTED

export const hasRejectedDocuments = (documents) =>
  documents.some(isRejectedByScan)

export const rejectedScans = (documents) =>
  scanned(documents.filter(isRejectedByScan))
claims.note: mechanism: these are read by the documents page and by the check-your-answers refusal, which part 17 and the check-answers part claim.

claims.statement: Only one error summary is ever shown: when the server has already rendered one, the oversize error is added to its list rather than a second summary appearing.
The oversize error in the summary is a link that takes the trader to the control they have to use to choose a different file.
claims.note: mechanism: a summary inserted after page load is initialised on the spot so its link focuses the field, with auto-focus left off because the page focuses the heading itself.

claims.statement: When the page carries no size limit or no oversize wording, or the limit is not a positive number, the browser makes no size check and the file is posted for the server to judge.

When a trader comes back to the documents page with the browser's Back or Forward button, the page is opened again from the service rather than shown from the browser's store, so the scan statuses are the current ones.
A trader who leaves the documents page while a scan is running and comes back to it finds the document settled, with its status shown as "Check completed" and a "View file" link on the row.

claims.statement: An uploaded document a trader views is served only under a content type the journey accepts for an upload, and anything else is served as plain bytes so the browser never renders it.
claims.note: mechanism: the content type is taken from the upload service's answer, cut at the first semicolon, trimmed and lower-cased before it is matched; the accepted set is PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, PNG, XLS and XLSX.

claims.statement: Nothing is announced to a screen-reader user when the page gives up asking for the scan statuses: the still-checking hint is unhidden but is not put in the live region.
claims.note: Looked in client/scan-status/poll.js, announce.js and the template's js-timeout-message paragraph: the hint is a govuk-hint with no aria-live, and showTimedOutHint() does not call announce().

claims.statement: The in-browser size check looks at the first file chosen only, so the page says nothing about the size of any later file a browser might hold on the field.
claims.quote:
const fileInput = form.querySelector('input[type="file"]')
  const file = fileInput?.files?.[0]
claims.note: Follows because only files[0] is read; the field is a single-file one, so this is a limit of the check rather than a defect a trader can reach today.

claims.statement: No fit spec proves the page reopens itself when the browser restores it from its back or forward store.

claims.statement: The browser asks the scan-status route for JSON.
Every usable answer the browser gets updates the rows it names straight away, before the browser decides whether to stop asking.
After each try the poll does one of three things: stops because every scan has settled, tries again, or gives up.
claims.note: mechanism: the decision the browser makes after each scan-status answer, from the attempt number and the documents returned.

claims.statement: Opening the documents page again once every scan has settled, or when the browser restores it from history, replaces the current history entry, so Back does not return to the stale copy of the page.
claims.quote:
globalThis.location.replace(href)
...
const openThisPageByGet = () =>
  globalThis.location.replace(globalThis.location.href)
claims.note: Follows because both use location.replace rather than assigning the location, which does not add a history entry.

claims.statement: When the page is opened again after the scans settle, it goes to the page's own GET address rather than reloading, because the page can also have been reached by a refused Continue post.
claims.quote:
// The page is also reachable by POST (a blocked
// Continue), so navigate to its GET href rather than reloading.
claims.note: The address is read from the announcer's data-settled-href; with none set, the page is not reopened.
